item.title: Version 1.0.14
item.description:
• Video feed (beta): show a live camera behind the prompter text, in the preview, the prompter window, or both. Any camera macOS sees works, including capture cards, Continuity Camera and virtual cameras such as Ecamm Live. Brightness, mirror, fill or fit, and a text drop shadow you can tune. Off by default; nothing is recorded. Buttons under the prompter, settings in the Video Feed section.
  • Settings in tabs: Follow, Companion, Updates and License, Help. A gear at the bottom right of the edit window opens and closes it.
  • Keyboard Shortcuts window: Help, Keyboard Shortcuts, also on the Help tab. Works offline.
  • Clearer help when a language is missing: the message now says how to install Apple's on-device model for your language.

item.title: Version 1.0.13
item.description:
• Highlighter: mark words with color blocks (yellow, green, cyan, pink, orange, purple, red) from the formatting bar. They show on the prompter, hug the words, and stay readable after you have read past them.
  • Marker number keys: press 1 to 9 to jump to that marker; the editor shows the spot too.
  • Arrow keys: Up and Down glide the prompter on a tap and scroll steadily while held; Left and Right step one line.

item.title: Version 1.0.12
item.description:
• Everything stays on screen in a small window: the formatting bar wraps onto more rows, the prompter preview can no longer be pushed off the window, and the window has a sensible minimum size.
  • Smooth preview resizing: dragging the divider beside the prompter preview no longer jumps or lags.
  • Bigger text in the markers panel: two buttons in the panel header make the marker names and snippets larger or smaller.
  • Park the editor timer anywhere: drag it off the script, onto the markers panel or to the far left edge.

item.title: Version 1.0.11
item.description:
• 24 more languages, in beta: Dutch, Danish, Swedish, Norwegian, Finnish, Polish, Russian, Turkish, Arabic, Hebrew, Hindi and more, recognized on your Mac with Apple's on-device dictation engine. Settings, Speech Recognition, "Language of the script". They are just as private; following may be less precise than in the main languages, so tell us how yours does.
  • Controls fit a narrow preview: the bar under the prompter preview rearranges itself instead of pushing buttons out of the window.
  • Status messages wrap instead of being cut off.

item.title: Version 1.0.10
item.description:
• Follow on macOS 27: fixes "Could not start audio input (error -10868)". When the normal audio route is refused, PowerCue retries with a fresh audio engine and then captures the microphone the way FaceTime does, so Follow works with every input.
  • A microphone that cannot start no longer stops Follow: PowerCue falls back to the system default input and says so in the status line.

item.title: Version 1.0.9
item.description: • Timer reset and close: hover the timer card for a reset button (elapsed back to 0:00) and a close button. The On-Screen Timer settings gain a Reset button too.

item.title: Version 1.0.8
item.description:
• Stumble and start again: re-read a line or paragraph you already read and the prompter jumps back to it. Prompter settings, Follow, "Jump back when I re-read a line" (on by default).
  • The phone microphone loses its dialog too: with PowerCue Companion 1.0.4 on iOS 26, the iPhone microphone uses the newer on-device speech engine and needs only the microphone permission.
  • Interruptions on the phone: a call or Siri taking the iPhone microphone is reported on the Mac, and listening resumes on its own when the microphone is free.

item.title: Version 1.0.7
item.description:
• No more "sent to Apple" dialog: on macOS 26 PowerCue uses Apple's newer on-device speech engine, which needs only the microphone permission. Speech never left your Mac before either; now the dialog that implied otherwise is gone.
  • Named markers: double-click a marker badge, or a row in the markers panel, to give it a name. The panel highlights the section the prompter is on.
  • Rearrange sections: drag a row in the markers panel (or right-click, Move Up / Move Down) and the whole block up to the next marker moves with it. Drag a badge in the text to move just the marker.
  • Paragraph gap: Text settings gain a switch and a slider for the space between paragraphs on the prompter; at zero, paragraphs sit right on top of each other. The Companion matches it (1.0.3).
  • Paste keeps your styling: pasted text takes the look of the text around the cursor instead of bringing its own fonts.

item.title: Version 1.0.6
item.description:
• Karaoke stays with your voice: the highlight now leads the recognizer so it sits on the word you are saying, glides at your reading pace between results, and when you pause it settles on the last word you said instead of running ahead. Prompter settings, Karaoke, Timing: Behind, In line or Ahead.
  • Fade and highlight are independent: dim what you have read without a highlight, or highlight without the fade.
  • Pill highlight: a rounded pill around the current word, with its own text color. Prompter settings, Karaoke, Style.
  • Which microphone is listening: while following, the status line under the prompter preview names the device. Recognition uses your system language and region.

item.title: Version 1.0.5
item.description:
• Run the prompter from your phone: PowerCue Companion 1.0.2 adds Follow, Play/Pause, Back to Top and marker buttons, and stays awake while prompting. If its microphone cannot listen, the phone says why.
  • Language of the script: Settings, Speech Recognition. Pick the language you read in; the Mac and the iPhone microphone both recognize it. Only on-device languages are offered.
  • The marker arrow is a handle: drag it to move the marker. It is bigger by default, goes much bigger, sits flush against the edge, and can live on the right side.

item.title: Version 1.0.4
item.description:
• Scroll from your phone: drag the script on the iPhone or iPad companion and the Mac prompter follows your finger. Play pauses while you drag and resumes where you let go; during Follow, letting go re-anchors the voice tracking right there. Needs PowerCue Companion 1.0.1 from the App Store.
  • Smarter crash reports: Send Crash Reports now attaches only reports from this app and this version (or the last week), each labeled with the version that crashed.
  • Companion sync is more robust when the script changes while a device is connected.

item.title: Version 1.0.3
item.description:
• PowerCue Companion is on the App Store: the free iPhone and iPad app that mirrors your prompter in lock-step and can act as your microphone. Settings now links straight to it, under iPhone & iPad Companion.
  • Small fixes and polish.

item.title: Version 1.0.2
item.description:
• PowerCue Companion for iPhone and iPad — mirror the prompter to your phone or tablet over local Wi-Fi, in perfect lock-step: same line breaks, styling, karaoke highlight, and on-screen timer. Turn it on under the display menu; the companion app is coming to the App Store.
  • Your iPhone as the microphone — pick "iPhone/iPad Microphone" in the mic menu and the phone in front of you drives voice following, with recognition staying on the device.
  • Prompter mode in the editor — the Prompter tab now styles the edit page exactly like the prompter (same line breaks, markers, timecodes) while staying a full text editor.
  • Font menu in the editor — the same font picker as the prompter, and Helvetica as the fresh-start default.
  • Timer button — show or hide the on-screen timer right from the control bar.
  • Voice following is more resilient — if macOS speech recognition fails mid-session, PowerCue now reconnects automatically instead of stalling.
  • A styled starter script that shows off markers and formatting, and assorted fixes.

item.title: Version 1.0.1
item.description:
• The prompter now leads you — the line you are about to read rests at the marker, so finishing a line advances the scroll immediately instead of waiting for your next word.
  • Voice following starts faster — and no longer drops words spoken across recognition boundaries, so it never loses you after a pause.
  • Play fixed at slow speeds — long run times and slow per-line speeds used to freeze the scroll in place; it now glides smoothly at any pace.
  • A guided tour — offered on first launch and replayable any time from Help → Take the Tour.
  • A real Settings window — microphone, automatic updates, help and feedback, and your license, under ⌘,.
  • Close toggles for the markers panel and the prompter preview, and a fresh starter script.

item.title: Version 1.0.0
item.description:
PowerCue 1.0 — the teleprompter that follows your voice.

  • Voice following with on-device speech recognition: pause and it waits, ad-lib and it re-anchors.
  • Karaoke highlight, jump markers, screen directions, and a fully styled dark-mode script editor.
  • Detachable prompter window with full mirror flips for beam-splitter rigs.
  • On-screen timer, run-time pacing with per-paragraph estimates, Word import and export.
